description: The bar chart illustrates the Shapley values, averaged over tasks, for three different models—mBERT (light blue), XLM-R (dark blue), and chLSTM (light green)—across various relative positions to a probed target word, labeled along the x-axis as L₄⁺, L₃, L₂, L₁, T, R₁, R₂, R₃, and R₄⁺, where “T” denotes the target word itself and “L” and “R” denote left and right context positions respectively. The y-axis represents the Shapley value, ranging from 0 to 80 with major gridlines at intervals of 20. The highest Shapley values occur at position T, where mBERT reaches approximately 60, XLM-R around 55, and chLSTM peaks at nearly 80. At position L₁, all three models show moderate contributions (mBERT and XLM-R around 15, chLSTM slightly higher). Contributions generally decrease moving away from the target, with L₂ and R₁ showing smaller values (around 5–10), and positions L₃, R₂, R₃, and R₄⁺ showing minimal or near-zero values. The bar for L₄⁺ is slightly elevated for mBERT and XLM-R (around 5–6), while chLSTM remains near zero. The chart visually emphasizes the dominance of the target token (T) and immediate left context (L₁) in contributing to model predictions, with chLSTM exhibiting the highest sensitivity at the target position. The bars are grouped by position, with each group containing three adjacent bars corresponding to the three models, and the legend in the top-right corner identifies each model by color.
